From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Subject: Re: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your message. I'm writing to dispute the $75 late fee added to my account for this month.

Rent was received on the 3rd, which falls within the grace period described in Section 4.2 of our lease. That section states that rent is due on the 1st, a grace period applies through the 5th, and no late fees may be charged during the grace period. Because the payment was made within that window, the fee does not appear to be permitted under the lease.

Please remove the $75 late fee from my account and confirm in writing that it has been reversed. I'd appreciate a response by [date].

Thank you for looking into this.

Best regards,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

A few tips:
- Keep a copy of your payment record showing the date it was received (check stub, money order receipt, or portal confirmation). If you paid through the portal, screenshot the confirmation.
- Since Section 9.4 allows email notices, sending it by email creates a written record. You could also send a copy by certified mail if the fee isn't reversed.
- If they refuse, you can usually bring this up with a local tenant rights organization or small claims court, depending on your state and the amount.
